page: Vultr vhp-8c-16gb-amd is a High Performance family virtual server built on the x86_64 architecture. It features an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz, configured with 8 vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core under a shared CPU allocation model. The system is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is provided by a bundled 350 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU hardware is present on this configuration.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core testing placing the server in the top 25% of tested instances. Multi-core CPU performance falls into the average category across stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and PassMark CPU tests. Memory bandwidth tests, including read-only and write operations on large uncached blocks, consistently register average performance. Database operations, such as Redis SET operations, and static web serving throughput also align with middle-tier performance expectations. For machine learning workloads, LLM inference using a medium 7B model shows average text generation speeds but weak prompt processing performance.

The shared CPU allocation represents a key architectural tradeoff, as resource sharing may introduce performance variability under sustained multi-core loads despite the strong single-core benchmark results. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the server offers a high-density configuration of 8 vCPUs and 350 GB of fast NVMe storage at a budget-friendly tier, making it a viable option for workloads that do not require dedicated CPU cores. This hardware profile is well-suited for general-purpose web serving, software compilation, medium-scale database operations, and lightweight text or image processing tasks.
